title: 2:30 AM on March 10, 2024 never happened in New York, but your code builds it anyway
assumption: Every combination of year/month/day/hour/minute you can type into a date constructor corresponds to a real moment in that timezone.

input.description: A scheduled reminder, cron-style job, or appointment time entered as a local wall-clock time on the day a timezone springs forward.

what_goes_wrong: A reminder set for 2:30 AM on the spring-forward day is silently given the pre-transition offset (-05:00), so it fires at 07:30 UTC, which the wall clock shows as 03:30 EDT -- and nothing tells you the time you asked for never existed.
why: On 2024-03-10 in America/New_York, clocks jump from 01:59:59 directly to 03:00:00, so every wall-clock time from 02:00 to 02:59 does not exist locally that day. Python's zoneinfo does not reject the construction. Under PEP 495, a time in a gap with the default fold=0 is interpreted with the offset in effect before the transition, so 02:30 gets -05:00 (EST) and converts to 07:30 UTC, which is 03:30 EDT on the wall clock; fold=1 would use the post-transition offset instead and give 06:30 UTC, which is 01:30 EST. The object itself keeps printing 02:30 until you round-trip it through UTC. JavaScript lands in the same place: ECMA-262 requires a skipped local time to be interpreted with the offset before the transition, so `new Date(2024, 2, 10, 2, 30)` in a process running in America/New_York is also 07:30 UTC. Neither language raises.

repros.code:
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
from datetime import datetime

tz = ZoneInfo("America/New_York")
gap = datetime(2024, 3, 10, 2, 30, tzinfo=tz)
print(gap, gap.utcoffset())
print(gap.astimezone(ZoneInfo("UTC")))

fix: Store and schedule in UTC; only render to local wall-clock at display time. If you must accept a local wall-clock input, detect the gap explicitly and surface it to the user rather than silently picking a side: with zoneinfo, a time is nonexistent when `dt.astimezone(timezone.utc).astimezone(tz).replace(tzinfo=None) != dt.replace(tzinfo=None)`; with pytz, `tz.localize(naive, is_dst=None)` raises `NonExistentTimeError`.
